A.note: Strongest is the disciplined refusal list that names exactly why each rejected metric is unsound; weakest is a query that leans on PERCENTILE_CONT WITHIN GROUP, COUNT(DISTINCT) in a windowed GROUP BY and INTO on a UNION branch, all of which it admits it cannot verify.

B.note: Strongest is the metric selection, which pairs latency, revision, intensity escalation and distinct-event rate into one coherent regional view; weakest is the reliance on COUNT(DISTINCT) inside a windowed GROUP BY, which it flags as unverified.

C.note: Strongest is the deliberately conservative syntax that avoids every construct it could not confirm, making it the most likely to run as written; weakest is grouping every metric by event_id in a ten-minute window, which leaves no cross-event or regional signal and gives most windows only one or two bulletins.

D.note: Strongest is the explicit reasoning for keeping event_id in the LAG partition but out of the window GROUP BY, which keeps the cross-event counts meaningful; weakest is the PERCENTILE_CONT OVER clause placed among aggregates in a tumbling GROUP BY, which it concedes may not compose.
